The cited paragraphs support the conclusion: p0084 obliges payment only of the fees set out in the Fee Schedule with no minimum, take-or-pay or shortfall construct; p0065 runs maintenance on a renewable one-year term rather than a locked multi-year commitment; and p0118 gives Sparkling (Customer) an unconditional 90-day termination right, providing the exit the rule requires. No deterministic checks fired and there is no directional error — the analysis correctly distinguishes license-scope/use restrictions (Authorized Locations, copy limits) from purchase-volume commitments, matching the rule's detection guidance. Minor, non-disqualifying: the rationale cites p0028 and Section 3 which are not among the supplied paragraphs, so those specific assertions are unverified; the compliance conclusion nonetheless rests adequately on the paragraphs provided.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We cannot accept a no-hire covering any employee of the other party, so we have narrowed this to a mutual non-solicitation limited to personnel directly involved in the services for 12 months from the end of their involvement, with the customary carve-outs for general advertisements and unsolicited approaches. Our preferred position is no non-solicit binding us at all, but we are content with this mutual narrowing.

ops.newText: During the term of this Agreement and for a period of twelve (12) months after the end of the relevant individual's involvement in the provision of services under this Agreement, neither party shall, and neither party shall permit its affiliates to, directly solicit for employment any employee of the other party who was directly involved in the provision of services under this Agreement. The foregoing shall not restrict either party or its affiliates from (i) placing or responding to general advertisements or recruitment campaigns that are not specifically targeted at the other party's personnel, or (ii) employing or engaging any person who approaches it on an unsolicited basis or who responds to such a general advertisement or campaign.
ops.oldText: During the term of this Agreement and for a period of one year thereafter, both parties agree not to hire or allow its respective affiliates to hire any employee of the other party, or any person who was an employee of the other party during the previous six months and who was directly involved in the provision of services under this Agreement.

proposal.summary: Convert mutual no-hire into a narrow 12-month mutual non-solicit limited to personnel directly involved in the services, with general-advertising and unsolicited-approach carve-outs.

quote: During the term of this Agreement and for a period of one year thereafter, both parties agree not to hire or allow its respective affiliates to hire any employee of the other party, or any person who was an employee of the other party during the previous six months and who was directly involved in the provision of services under this Agreement.
rationale: Section 19 binds us (as well as the Vendor) with an outright no-hire — "not to hire or allow its respective affiliates to hire" — which is a walk-away item under the playbook, and it extends to "any employee of the other party" rather than only personnel involved in the services. There is also no carve-out for general advertisements or unsolicited approaches, and the restricted period runs from termination of the Agreement rather than from the end of the individual's involvement. Because the covenant is already mutual, we have taken the fallback: a 12-month mutual non-solicit limited to personnel directly involved in the services, with general-advertising and unsolicited-approach carve-outs and the no-hire deleted.

checks.detail: changed-character ratio=0.748 (advisory: whole-clause rewrites are acceptable when the rule requires them)
checks.name: minimal edit p0133

verification.notes: The rule's walk-away trigger is correctly identified: original p0133 is a no-hire ('not to hire or allow its respective affiliates to hire') covering 'any employee of the other party' with no general-advertising carve-out, so the deviation status is accurate. The redline lands squarely on the playbook fallback: mutual non-solicit only, scope limited to personnel directly involved in the services, 12 months measured from the end of the individual's involvement, and express carve-outs for general advertisements/recruitment campaigns and unsolicited approaches; the no-hire language is deleted. Mutuality is preserved ('neither party shall, and neither party shall permit its affiliates to'), so the edit does not create a one-sided obligation, and it is directionally favorable to the Customer. The failed 'minimal edit' heuristic (0.748 changed-character ratio) is justified here — converting a no-hire into a narrowed non-solicit with new carve-outs necessarily requires rewriting the sentence; no smaller edit would remove the hire prohibition and add the carve-out. Comment is accurate, concise, in first person plural with the [Playbook] prefix, states what changed and why, cites the preferred position (no non-solicit) and accepts the fallback.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] Section 10 refers to a "renewable one-year term" but sets out no renewal mechanics or limit on maintenance fee increases, so we have added automatic twelve-month renewals that we may exit on 30 days' notice, a 60-day renewal reminder from Garman, and an uplift cap at the lesser of CPI and 3%. If a cap at that level is difficult, we can accept a 60-day non-renewal window and a 5% ceiling.

ops.text: (d) RENEWAL OF MAINTENANCE TERM. The maintenance term shall renew automatically for successive terms of twelve (12) months each, unless Sparkling gives Garman written notice of non-renewal not less than thirty (30) calendar days before the end of the then-current maintenance term. Garman shall give Sparkling written notice of the upcoming renewal, including any proposed change in maintenance fees, not less than sixty (60) calendar days before the end of the then-current maintenance term. Maintenance fees for any renewal term shall not exceed the fees payable for the then-current term increased by the lesser of (i) the percentage increase in the Consumer Price Index over the preceding twelve (12) months and (ii) three percent (3%).

proposal.summary: Add maintenance renewal mechanics: automatic 12-month renewals, 30-day customer opt-out, 60-day vendor renewal/price notice, uplift capped at lesser of CPI and 3%.

quote: For a renewable one-year term commencing upon the Maintenance Commencement Date, subject to payment of maintenance fees in accordance with the Fee Schedule but without additional fees or charges, Garman shall provide the following Maintenance Services:
rationale: Section 10 contemplates a "renewable one-year term" for Maintenance Services but the Agreement contains no renewal mechanics: there is no auto-renewal or mutual-agreement provision, no non-renewal notice window, no vendor renewal reminder, and Section 11/the Fee Schedule impose no cap on maintenance fee uplift at renewal. That leaves renewal pricing and continuity entirely undetermined and exposes us to unbounded increases. Added a renewal clause matching the preferred position (automatic 12-month renewals, 30-day customer opt-out, 60-day Garman reminder, uplift capped at the lesser of CPI and 3%), with the 60-day/5% fallback flagged in the comment.

verification.notes: The gap is real: p0065 references a "renewable one-year term" for Maintenance Services but the Agreement supplies no renewal trigger, non-renewal notice window, reminder or fee-uplift cap, so a 'missing' classification under RENEWAL is correct. The inserted subsection reaches the preferred position precisely: automatic successive 12-month terms, Customer (Sparkling) opt-out on 30 days' written notice, Garman renewal/price-change reminder 60 days before term end, and renewal fees capped at the lesser of CPI over the preceding 12 months and 3%. Placement is sensible — the clause is appended at the end of the Section 10 maintenance provisions (p0082, last item of the exclusions list) rather than in the fees section, keeping renewal mechanics with the maintenance term; only minor risk is that the manual "(d)" label could collide with existing lettering and should be checked on execution. The deterministic failure on "non-renewal notice window ≤ 60 days" is a regex phrasing artifact: the drafted text does specify "not less than thirty (30) calendar days before the end of the then-current maintenance term," which satisfies the ≤30-day preferred window. Comment is accurate, concise, in the required voice and prefix, explains what changed and why, and correctly offers the fallback (60-day window, 5% ceiling) without overreaching.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have moved our convenience termination notice from ninety (90) to thirty (30) days and added a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees, consistent with our position that the customer may exit on 30 days' notice without penalty. If Garman needs a longer wind-down, we can live with 60 days' notice provided the refund of prepaid fees remains.

ops.newText: (b) Sparkling may terminate this Agreement, in whole or in part, at any time for convenience upon thirty (30) calendar days written notice to Garman. If Sparkling terminates this Agreement pursuant to this Section 17(b), Sparkling shall cease using the Software at the end of the thirty (30) day notice period, and shall certify to Garman within thirty (30) calendar days of termination that Sparkling has destroyed or has returned to Garman all Software, Documentation and Codes. No termination charge, penalty or early termination fee shall be payable in respect of such termination, and Garman shall refund to Sparkling, within thirty (30) calendar days of the effective date of termination, any fees prepaid in respect of any period after that date.
ops.oldText: (b) Sparkling may terminate this Agreement at any time upon ninety (90) calendar days written notice to Garman. If Sparkling terminates this Agreement pursuant to this Section 17(b), Sparkling shall cease using the Software at the end of the ninety (90) day notice period, and shall certify to Garman within thirty (30) calendar days of termination that Sparkling has destroyed or has returned to Garman all Software, Documentation and Codes.

proposal.summary: Shorten Sparkling's convenience termination notice to 30 days and add pro-rata refund of prepaid fees

quote: (b) Sparkling may terminate this Agreement at any time upon ninety (90) calendar days written notice to Garman.
rationale: Section 17(b) does give us a convenience right and Garman has no reciprocal at-will right (Garman may terminate only for insolvency or uncured material default under 17(c)), so the direction of the clause is acceptable. However, the notice period is 90 days (fallback, not preferred 30 days) and, unlike the default/rejection remedies in Sections 8 and 17(c), the clause is silent on any refund of prepaid fees, so we could pay for licence and maintenance periods we no longer use. Redline shortens notice to 30 days and adds a no-penalty, pro-rata refund of prepaid fees; 60 days' notice is an acceptable fallback if the refund is retained.

checks.name: minimal edit p0118

verification.notes: Directionally correct for the Customer (Sparkling): notice for our convenience termination is cut from 90 to 30 days, matching the preferred position, and the wind-down/certification timing is conformed consistently. The added sentence supplies the two missing preferred-position elements — no termination charge/early-termination fee and a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees — using language close to the model clause, with no expansion of Garman's rights. The failed deterministic check 'Customer convenience termination present' appears to be a phrasing-match artifact; the revised text expressly states 'Sparkling may terminate this Agreement, in whole or in part, at any time for convenience upon thirty (30) calendar days written notice', so the substance is satisfied. The 0.434 changed-character ratio is justified by the required refund/no-penalty addition. Comment is accurate, concise, in first person plural, correctly cites the playbook position, and offers the 60-day notice fallback conditioned on retaining the refund. Rationale correctly recognises that Garman has no reciprocal at-will right (Section 17(c) limited to insolvency/uncured default), so no deletion of a Vendor convenience right is needed and the edit remains the smallest change reaching the preferred position.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have added an exit clause at Section 17(d): on any expiry or termination Garman provides up to six months of transition assistance at its then-current rates, returns our data in a machine-readable format within thirty days, and then deletes it and certifies deletion. The Agreement currently obliges only Sparkling to return/destroy materials on termination (Section 17(b)) and is silent on the return of our converted data under Section 4(b), which leaves us unable to migrate; we can accept 90 days of assistance as a fallback.

ops.text: (d) Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Garman shall (1) at Sparkling's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Garman's then-current rates; (2) within thirty (30) calendar days of such expiry or termination, return to Sparkling all of Sparkling's data in Garman's possession or control, including all data converted pursuant to Section 4(b), in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (3) thereafter delete all such data from its systems and certify such deletion to Sparkling in writing.

proposal.summary: Insert new Section 17(d) requiring Garman to provide transition assistance, return Sparkling's data in machine-readable form within 30 days, and certify deletion.

quote: (b) Sparkling may terminate this Agreement at any time upon ninety (90) calendar days written notice to Garman. If Sparkling terminates this Agreement pursuant to this Section 17(b), Sparkling shall cease using the Software at the end of the ninety (90) day notice period, and shall certify to Garman within thirty (30) calendar days of termination that Sparkling has destroyed or has returned to Garman all Software, Documentation and Codes.
rationale: Section 17 addresses only Sparkling's obligation to cease use and return/destroy Garman's Software, Documentation and Codes; there is no exit-assistance obligation and no requirement for Garman to return our data (including data converted under Section 4(b)) or to delete and certify deletion. Section 14 imposes only confidentiality obligations, and Section 18 survival lists nothing on transition or data return. Searches for "transition" and "data" confirm the absence. Inserted a new Section 17(d) matching the preferred position: six months of transition assistance at then-current rates, return of our data in a machine-readable format within thirty days, and subsequent deletion with written certification.
ruleTitle: Post-termination transition assistance and data return

verification.notes: Missing-clause finding is substantiated: Section 17(b) only obliges Sparkling (us) to cease use and return/destroy Garman's Software, Documentation and Codes, and the survival list (Section 18) contains nothing on exit assistance or data return, so the agreement is silent on Garman returning our data or providing migration help. Direction is correct for our side: the inserted 17(d) places the obligations on Garman (Vendor/Licensor) and runs in favour of Sparkling (Customer/Licensee), including the data converted under Section 4(b). Insert tracks the preferred position closely and completely — up to six months of transition assistance at then-current rates, return of data in a commonly used machine-readable format within thirty days, and subsequent deletion with written certification — with no extraneous edits to existing text (minimal-edit test met). Placement as a new subsection (d) within Section 17 (Term and Termination), after 17(b)/(c) and before the survival provision, matches the redline guidance; the survival clause is non-exhaustive ("include but are not limited to") and expressly covers provisions contemplating post-termination performance, so no conforming amendment there is strictly necessary. Comment is accurate, concise, first-person plural, cites the playbook position, explains the gap (silence on our converted data under Section 4(b)) and offers the 90-day fallback without lecturing. Minor, non-blocking: the anchor paragraph p0129 is shown as "not yet rendered," so exact adjacency/lettering (assumes p0129 is 17(c)) should be confirmed on final rendering; optionally add Section 17(d) to the Section 18 survival enumeration for belt-and-braces.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] Section 12 gives us a twelve-month conformance warranty but no stated remedy and no warranty covering Garman's services, legal compliance or malicious code. We have added a professional and workmanlike standard for the Services, a repair/replace/refund remedy for breach, and standard compliance-with-laws and no-malicious-code warranties, consistent with our playbook position.

ops.text: Garman further warrants that: (a) all Services (including installation, data conversion, training and Maintenance Services) will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards, and for a period of ninety (90) days following performance will conform in all material respects to the applicable Specifications and Documentation; (b) it will comply with all laws applicable to its performance under this Agreement; and (c) the Software as delivered will be free of any virus, worm, time bomb, disabling device or other malicious code. If any Software, Deliverable or Service fails to conform to the warranties in this Section 12, Garman shall promptly repair, replace or re-perform the non-conforming item at no charge to Sparkling and, if Garman fails to do so within thirty (30) days of written notice, Garman shall refund the fees paid for the non-conforming Software, Deliverable or Service.

proposal.summary: Add services warranty, express warranty remedy (repair/replace/refund), compliance with laws and no malicious code to Section 12

quote: For the acceptance period and for a period of one year from the Maintenance Commencement Date, and thereafter for as long as the Software is covered by Maintenance Services and is used by Sparkling in accordance with this Agreement, Garman warrants that the Software shall perform in conformance with the Specifications in all material respects.
rationale: The software conformance warranty duration (one year from the Maintenance Commencement Date, extended while under Maintenance) meets the preferred 12-month position, and there is no implied-warranty disclaimer anywhere in the Agreement, so the express warranty is not swallowed. However, Section 12 states no remedy for breach: the only warranty-adjacent remedies are the acceptance-period rejection right in Sections 7-8 (time-limited and "in lieu of any other remedy") and Software Repair Service under Section 10(c), which is only a "best efforts" obligation conditional on a paid maintenance subscription. There is also no warranty that Garman's services (installation, data conversion, training, maintenance) will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner, no compliance-with-laws warranty, and no no-malicious-code warranty. We therefore insert a single supplemental paragraph in Section 12 adding the services standard, a repair/replace/re-perform-or-refund remedy, compliance with laws and no malicious code, leaving the existing 12-month software warranty intact.

checks.name: warranty period ≥ 90 days or expressed in months/years

verification.notes: The claimed deviation is substantiated: p0086 supplies a 12-month software conformance warranty but no remedy, no professional-and-workmanlike services standard, no compliance-with-laws warranty and no no-malicious-code warranty, all of which the WARRANTY preferred position requires. The redline is minimal and additive — the existing 12-month warranty sentence is left untouched and a single supplemental paragraph inserts the missing elements (services standard, 90-day conformance, repair/replace/re-perform with refund backstop, legal compliance, no malicious code), matching the model language closely enough. Direction is correct for the customer: remedies and additional warranties run in our favour, and no vendor-favourable concession is introduced. Comment is accurate and appropriately scoped (it says Section 12 states no remedy, which is true; the acceptance-period and best-efforts repair rights noted in the rationale are elsewhere in the agreement), uses the [Playbook] prefix and the required concise first-person-plural tone. Deterministic checks both pass (operation applies; warranty period expressed in months/days ≥ 90 days), consistent with the substantive review.

quote: Confidential Information means all data and information related to the business and management of either party, including proprietary and trade secrets, technology and accounting records for which access is obtained by the other party pursuant to this Agreement, provided that such Confidential Information shall not include data or information which:
rationale: Compliant: no audit, inspection, records-examination or usage-verification right runs against Sparkling anywhere in the Agreement, and Garman has no right of access to Sparkling systems. Searches for "audit", "inspect", "verify", "records", "premises", "monitor", "report" and "certif" return nothing operative. Addressing the two residual points: (1) § 14 read in full (p0094-p0101) is a purely mutual definitional clause - the phrase "accounting records for which access is obtained by the other party pursuant to this Agreement" is descriptive of the scope of Confidential Information and is conditioned on access obtained under some other provision; § 14 contains only the definition and the six standard carve-outs (a)-(f), with no entry, examination, delivery or access mechanism, and § 1(b) simply cross-refers the definition to § 14. (2) The Schedules are incorporated by p0019 ("The following is a summary of the Schedules, which shall form an integral part of this Agreement") but appear in the text only as titles - Fee Schedule; Software and Documentation; Authorized Locations and Software copies; Specifications, Modifications, Data Conversion; Implementation and Training; Telephone Support - none of which is a reporting, certification or verification schedule, and no operative clause (including § 11, which is a bare obligation to pay the Fee Schedule fees) imports any usage-reporting or true-up right from them. § 3 imposes substantive use limits only; § 20 is time-of-the-essence and notices boilerplate; § 17(b) is a one-off post-termination self-certification of destruction/return with no vendor entry, auditor or system access. Because no audit right binds us, the AUDIT parameters (frequency, notice, cost allocation, system access) cannot arise, and the absence of any such right is at least as favorable as the playbook preferred position. Inserting frequency/notice/cost machinery would create a new Customer obligation and enlarge Garman's rights, so the correct minimal action is no edit.

verification.notes: audit frequency limited: failed Claimed status is 'compliant' by absence of any audit right binding the Customer, and the supplied paragraphs support that: none of p0019, p0035, p0084, p0095, p0118 or p0134 grants Garman inspection, examination, entry, usage-reporting or system-access rights. The two potential hooks are correctly dispositioned: the § 14 reference to 'accounting records for which access is obtained ... pursuant to this Agreement' is definitional and mutual, conditioned on access granted elsewhere (no such grant exists), and § 17(b) is a one-off post-termination self-certification by Sparkling with no vendor entry or auditor involvement. No redline and no counterparty comment is the expected and correct output for a compliant finding; inserting frequency/notice/cost machinery would create a Customer obligation and manufacture a vendor audit right that does not exist, so 'no edit' is the minimal correct action. The failed deterministic check ('audit frequency limited') is a false signal here — the regex looks for frequency-capping language that is unnecessary where no audit right exists; absence of any audit right is at least as favorable as the preferred position. Rationale is internally consistent with the quoted text and does not overstate; no directional error detected.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] The Agreement contains no insurance provision, yet Garman's personnel attend our sites for installation and training and Garman handles conversion of Sparkling's data, so we have added our standard coverages (CGL USD 1M/2M, E&O USD 2M, cyber USD 5M, statutory workers' compensation) with certificates on request. If USD 5M cyber is not available, we can accept E&O of USD 1M and cyber of USD 2M as a fallback.

ops.text: Garman shall maintain, at its own expense, throughout the term of this Agreement and for one (1) year thereafter: commercial general liability insurance of not less than USD 1,000,000 per occurrence and USD 2,000,000 in the aggregate; professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance of not less than USD 2,000,000; cyber liability insurance of not less than USD 5,000,000 covering Garman's access to or processing of Sparkling's data; and workers' compensation insurance as required by applicable law. Garman shall provide Sparkling with certificates of insurance evidencing such coverage on request.

proposal.summary: Insert standard vendor insurance covenant as new General Matters subsection (j)

quote: (i) All paragraph headings contained in this Agreement are for convenience only and shall not affect the interpretation of this Agreement.
rationale: A document-wide search for "insurance" returns no results, and General Matters (sec-20, continuing to p0147) ends with headings without any insurance covenant. Garman personnel attend Authorized Locations for installation and training (sec-4, sec-5) and convert Sparkling's data, so the playbook requires standard coverages. Inserted a new subsection (j) after the last General Matters subsection with CGL USD 1M/2M, E&O USD 2M, cyber USD 5M for processing of Sparkling's data, statutory workers' compensation, and certificates on request; fallback of E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M offered in the comment.

verification.notes: Correctly identified a missing insurance clause: no insurance covenant appears in the cited General Matters section, and the vendor (Garman) both attends Customer sites and converts Sparkling's data, so the rule's trigger is satisfied. Inserted language matches the playbook preferred position in full — CGL USD 1M/2M, E&O USD 2M, cyber USD 5M tied to processing of Sparkling's data, statutory workers' compensation, certificates on request, and survival for one year post-term — and is directionally correct (obligation on Garman, benefit to Sparkling). Comment is accurate, concise, in the required voice with the [Playbook] prefix, and offers the sanctioned fallback (E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M). Minor drafting nit (not disqualifying): the rationale states a new lettered subsection (j) was added, but the rendered insert carries no '(j)' label and follows the headings subsection (i) as an unlabeled sentence; adding the '(j)' designator would keep the clause from reading as part of the headings provision.
